test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 9 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT in the list of five Sikh Takhts?

options.text: Sri Damdama Sahib, Talwandi Sabo, Bathinda
Shri Rakab Ganj Sahib, New Delhi

solution:
The correct answer is __**Shri Rakab Ganj Sahib, New Delhi**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In Sikhism, the **Takhts** are the five highest seats of authority and are considered significant spiritual and historical centers.
 
• Each Takht has its own unique importance and history
 
• **Shri Rakab Ganj Sahib** is a significant religious site within Sikhism, it is not classified as one of the five Takhts, which serve as the central authoritative bodies for decision-making and governance within the Sikh community.
 
• **Shri Rakab Ganj Sahib is located **in New Delhi.
 
• It is an important Gurdwara that c**ommemorates the martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, the ninth Guru,** who was executed for defending the religious freedom of Hindus against Mughal oppression.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sri Akal Takht Sahib:**

 
 
• **Location: Amritsar, Punjab**
 
• The Akal Takht is the **highest of the five Takhts** and serves as the spiritual and temporal authority of Sikhism.
 
• It was **established by Guru Hargobind Ji, the sixth Guru, in 1606.**
 
• The Akal Takht is closely **associated with the Golden Temple** (Harmandir Sahib) and represents the central place for making important decisions affecting the Sikh community.
 
 
 
• **Sri Keshgarh Sahib**:
 
 
• **Location: Anandpur Sahib, Punjab**
 
• This Takht was** established by Guru Gobind Singh Ji, the tenth Guru, in 1709.**
 
• It is the birthplace of the Khalsa, the collective body of initiated Sikhs.
 
• Keshgarh Sahib is a site of immense historical importance, especially regarding the f**ormation of the Khalsa Panth.**
 
 
 
• **Sri Damdama Sahib**:
 
 
• **Location: Talwandi Sabo, Bathinda, Punjab**
 
• This Takht is where **Guru Gobind Singh Ji compiled the Zafarnama (a letter of victory) and finalized the Guru Granth Sahib.**
 
• It is also where the Guru spent significant time during his life, making it an important place for Sikhs.
 
 
 
• **Sri Patna Sahib**:
 
 
• **Location: Patna, Bihar**
 
• **This Takht is the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh Ji.**
 
• It holds significant historical and religious importance, as it is associated with the life of the tenth Guru and the establishment of the Khalsa.
 
 
 
• **Sri Hazur Sahib**:
 
 
• Location: Nanded, Maharashtra
 
• This Takht is where **Guru Gobind Singh Ji passed away in 1708.**
 
• It is a major pilgrimage site for Sikhs and is where the Guru declared the Guru Granth Sahib as the eternal Guru of the Sikhs.
